record.original_question: For each integer k >= 3, determine the infimum alpha(k) such that every graph G of order n = Omega(k^alpha) with lambda(G) > lambda(S^+_{n,k}) contains a cycle C_{2k+2}.

evidence.quote: Problem 2 (A refined version of Nikiforov’s even cycle conjecture [94]). For any integer k ≥ 3, determine the infimum α := α(k) such that every graph of order n = Ω(k^α) satisfying λ(G) > λ(S^+_{n,k}) contains a C_{2k+2}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For integers $n > k \geq 1$, let $S_{n,k}$ denote the graph obtained as the join of a complete graph $K_k$ on $k$ vertices with an independent set on $n-k$ vertices, and let $S_{n,k}^{+}$ denote the graph obtained from $S_{n,k}$ by adding one extra edge inside the independent set. For a graph $G$, let $\lambda(G)$ denote the largest eigenvalue (spectral radius) of its adjacency matrix, and let $C_{\ell}$ denote the cycle of length $\ell$.

For each integer $k \geq 3$, determine the infimum value $\alpha(k)$ such that the following statement holds: there exists a constant $c = c(k) > 0$ such that every graph $G$ on $n \geq c\, k^{\alpha(k)}$ vertices satisfying
$$\lambda(G) > \lambda(S_{n,k}^{+})$$
contains $C_{2k+2}$ as a subgraph.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open problem (a refined version of Nikiforov's even cycle conjecture) in a 2023 survey of unsolved problems in spectral graph theory. While the original Nikiforov even cycle conjecture has been resolved for sufficiently large $n$, the refined quantitative question of determining the optimal threshold exponent $\alpha(k)$ does not appear to have been settled in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Unsolved Problems in Spectral Graph Theory

status_evidence.title: The spectral even cycle problem
status_evidence.snippet: Resolves Nikiforov's even cycle conjecture for sufficiently large n, but does not determine the sharp threshold exponent in k.
status_evidence.claim: Original Nikiforov conjecture solved for large n, but the refined quantitative exponent question is not addressed.
